item.title: GSTAT Allows Leniency in Appeal Scrutiny Until July 2026
item.description: GST Appellate Tribunal has issued an order allowing lenient scrutiny of appeal documents on the GSTAT Portal for six months, limiting objections to substantive defects only. The post GSTAT Allows Leniency in Appeal Scrutiny Until July 2026 appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas Advises QSR Asia and RBA on Lenexis Acquisition
item.description: The transaction involves a significant stake sale, preferential allotment, and a mandatory open offer, marking a major shift in the company’s ownership structure. The post Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas Advises QSR Asia and RBA on Lenexis Acquisition appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Noncompete covenant not binding on non-signatory employee/third-party organiser; Bombay HC deines relief to Messe Frankfurt
item.description: “There were no traceable clandestine or fraudulent activities by Netlink and its Director in organising the impugned exhibitions for the ostensible organiser, and therefore it was unnecessary to undertake the exercise of lifting the corporate veil or applying group of companies doctrine.” The post Noncompete covenant not binding on non-signatory employee/third-party organiser; Bombay HC deines relief to Messe Frankfurt appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas advised Bessemer Venture Partners on its investment in Sukino Healthcare Solutions Private Limited.
item.description: The transaction involved a combination of primary investment and secondary acquisition from existing investors, including Stakeboat Capital, reflecting continued investor interest in India’s healthcare services sector. The post Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas advised Bessemer Venture Partners on its investment in Sukino Healthcare Solutions Private Limited. appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: DNA doesn’t lie! Delhi HC upholds POCSO Conviction of father who impregnated minor daughter
item.description: “The social circumstances and the economic status of the family may have compelled the Prosecutrix and her mother to give contradictory statements or to turn hostile. However, in such cases the Court cannot completely ignore the scientific evidence which has come on record.” The post DNA doesn’t lie! Delhi HC upholds POCSO Conviction of father who impregnated minor daughter appeared first on SCC Times.
